Description:
The Splunk Add-on for AWS, from version 7.0.0 and above, includes a merge of all the capabilities of the Splunk Add-on for Amazon Security Lake. This allows you to configure the Splunk Add-on for AWS to ingest data across all AWS data sources, facilitating the integration of AWS data into your Splunk platform deployment. If you use both the Splunk Add-on for Amazon Security Lake as well as the Splunk Add-on for AWS on the same Splunk instance, then you must uninstall the Splunk Add-on for Amazon Security Lake before upgrading the Splunk Add-on for AWS to version 7.0.0 or later in order to avoid any data duplication and discrepancy issues. __________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Ingesting data from AWS to Splunk Cloud? Have you tried the new Splunk Data Manager yet? Data Manager makes AWS data ingestion simpler, more automated and centrally managed for you, while co-existing with AWS and/or Kinesis TAs. Read our blog post to learn more about Data Manager and it’s availability on your Splunk Cloud instance: https://splk.it/3e9F863 __________________________________________________________________________________________________________ The Splunk Add-on for Amazon Web Services allows a Splunk software administrator to collect: * Configuration snapshots, configuration changes, and historical configuration data from the AWS Config service. * Metadata for your AWS EC2 instances, reserved instances, and EBS snapshots. * Compliance details, compliance summary, and evaluation status of your AWS Config Rules. * Assessment Runs and Findings data from the Amazon Inspector service. * Management and change events from the AWS CloudTrail service. * VPC flow logs and other logs from the CloudWatch Logs service. * Performance and billing metrics from the AWS CloudWatch service. * Billing reports that you have configured in AWS. * S3, CloudFront, and ELB access logs. * Generic data from your S3 buckets. * Generic data from your Kinesis streams. * Generic data from SQS. * Security events from Amazon Security Lake This add-on provides modular inputs and CIM-compatible knowledge to use with other apps, such as the Splunk App for AWS, Splunk Enterprise Security and Splunk IT Service Intelligence. Versions 5.0.0 and later of the Splunk Add-on for AWS is compatible only with Splunk Enterprise version 8.0.0 and above.

item.title: Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk - v3.2.42 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
##### Catalyst Center Reports * **Compliance report sourcetype routing fixed:** Some Catalyst Center compliance reports, including `NetworkDeviceComplianceDaily`, were incorrectly indexed as the generic `cisco:catalyst:center:report` sourcetype because their broad `dataCategory` was `Network`. Classification now evaluates specific report/view names and IDs before broad category metadata. Compliance reports route to `cisco:catalyst:center:compliance:report`, inventory reports route to `cisco:catalyst:center:inventory:report`, and all other report categories route to `cisco:catalyst:center:report` with `report_category`. This restores the expected data source for Network Compliance dashboards and searches. * **Automatic discovery added and highly recommended:** The Reports input can now enumerate Catalyst Center on every poll and collect all current reports plus reports created later. Enable **Automatically collect all reports (Recommended)** for most deployments. The older **Select all** action remains a fixed snapshot and does not automatically include reports created after the input is saved. * **Report configuration and flow are visible in Data Collection Health:** The Catalyst Center tab now shows each configured Reports input, enabled state, automatic/fixed/legacy mode, configured scope, observed report names and categories, resulting sourcetypes, event count, and latest event in the selected window. ##### Platform and compatibility * **Splunk 10.6 / Python 3.13 readiness:** Added `python.required = 3.13` on all 28 modular inputs and 42 REST handler stanzas so Splunk 10.2+ can select the Python 3.13 runtime. Retained `python.version = python3` on all stanzas for Splunk 10.0/10.1 compatibility (`python.required` is ignored on those releases). ##### Custom API endpoint catalogs * **Recommended-by-default endpoint picker:** SD-WAN and Catalyst Center Custom API inputs now open with **Recommended only** enabled. This keeps routine observability reads focused while allowing administrators to turn the filter off and browse the broader safe GET catalog. **Show live-checked only** remains off by default so valid endpoints are not hidden merely because they were not part of the representative live-check sample. * **SD-WAN catalog expanded safely:** Expanded the catalog to the full allow-listed set of safe, parameter-free vManage GET endpoints, tiered into Recommended and Advanced views. The picker displays the current Recommended and total available endpoint counts from the installed catalog. Certificate status (`/dataservice/certificate/list/status`), certificate detail (`/dataservice/certificate/stats/detail`), and certificate expiration status (`/dataservice/certificate/stats/summary`) are included in the Recommended view. * **SD-WAN operational safeguards:** Excluded request-body, path-templated, deprecated, API-introspection, heavy duplicate, dedicated-input overlap, `/dataservice/device/action/*`, and action-like GET operations. The expanded view remains an allow-list and never becomes an arbitrary-URL collector. * **Catalyst Center catalog expanded and tiered:** The catalog now includes the full allow-listed safe GET surface from the installed OpenAPI catalog, tiered into Recommended observability reads and Advanced configuration or operational reads. The picker displays the current Recommended and total available endpoint counts. Credential-configuration, count-only, deprecated, path-templated, and dedicated-input overlap endpoints remain excluded. * **Live-check behavior scaled for larger catalogs:** REST handlers live-check a representative sample of Recommended endpoints instead of probing every catalog entry. Selecting an untested endpoint runs a targeted check, and the handlers report current Recommended and total available counts to the UI. * **Existing inputs remain editable:** When an existing input uses an Advanced endpoint, the picker automatically reveals the broader catalog so the saved selection is not hidden. ##### Dashboards and usability * **User Guide package-version SPL hardened for Splunk 10.6:** Updated the live package-version REST search to use Splunk 10.6-compatible `if()` boolean logic, rename dotted REST fields to `current_version` and `latest_version`, and compute `update_status` with nested `if()` instead of `case()`. * **Custom API guidance expanded:** Added operator guidance for Recommended and Advanced endpoint tiers, certificate monitoring, targeted live checks, load review, safe starting intervals, and the exclusions that protect controllers from operational actions. * **Duplicate-input detection across all API products:** Data Collection Health now correlates product, normalized remote-system identity, sourcetype, input stanza, account, destination index, and collector host. Overview provides a consolidated detector, while Catalyst Center, Cyber Vision, SD-WAN, and ISE each provide a focused panel. This detects both duplicate stanzas on one heavy forwarder and the same collection path configured on multiple heavy forwarders, including inputs that use different account labels or destination indexes. * **Collector hosts and installed TA releases are visible without REST:** Overview and every product tab, including Network Syslog, now identify the Splunk hosts onboarding or processing Cisco data. Forwarded structured poll logs report the locally installed TA version/build and authoritative modular-input owner; sampled `per_sourcetype_thruput` metrics add processed event, KB/s, EPS, event-age, and pipeline-latency evidence. Passive syslog rows identify the receiving indexer and explicitly note that an intermediate heavy-forwarder identity is not preserved in the events. * **Operational tables are easier to scan:** Repeated TA internal-log events collapse into one row per input with an occurrence count and latest diagnostics. Onboarding-host tables use larger text, stable column widths, horizontal scrolling, numeric alignment, and trimmed long evidence lists with hover text instead of producing extremely tall rows. * **Dashboard reliability and information dialogs improved:** Fixed the shared duplicate-detector query so Dashboard Studio token parsing cannot corrupt regular-expression anchors, eliminating the related search failures across all tabs. Information dialogs no longer show a duplicate divider above their first section while retaining separators between later sections. ##### Collector telemetry * **Local release metadata on structured TA logs:** Canonical TA log events now include `ta_version` and `ta_build`, read from the add-on installation on the collector itself. Search-time extractions make those fields available to Data Collection Health, allowing a search head to reveal heavy-forwarder release drift without calling Splunk REST. * **SD-WAN remote-system identity preserved:** SD-WAN energy-stat events now retain `vmanage_host` independently from the managed-device `host` field so duplicate detection can identify the actual vManage collection target. * **Evidence boundaries are explicit:** A processing-only `metrics.log` host may be a heavy forwarder or an indexer, and `per_sourcetype_thruput` is top-N sampled. An installed but idle host that emits no TA telemetry still requires deployment inventory or authenticated REST to prove. ##### Maintenance * **Input spec consistency test updated:** Added `python.required` to the standard `inputs.conf` keys validated by `test_inputs_spec_consistency.py`. * **Endpoint catalog regression coverage:** Added catalog-builder and REST-handler tests for recommendation counts, sensitive and operational exclusions, representative probing, targeted probing, and response metadata. The full modular-input smoke suite continues to validate all Cisco product inputs. * **Health-dashboard regression coverage expanded:** Added tests for cross-product duplicate identity, collector/version evidence, processing metrics, per-input log aggregation, table readability, and the first-section information-dialog divider behavior. ##### Upgrade notes * No reconfiguration required; existing accounts, inputs, and KV Store checkpoints are preserved. * Existing Reports input stanzas are preserved and do not need to be deleted or recreated. Legacy named-report fields and fixed multi-select configurations continue to work. * For ongoing report coverage, edit the Reports input and enable **Automatically collect all reports (Recommended)**. Saved fixed selections remain stored and are restored if automatic mode is later disabled. * Corrected sourcetype routing applies to newly collected events. Events already indexed under `cisco:catalyst:center:report` are not rewritten; account for the historical generic sourcetype in temporary searches until corrected compliance events arrive. * Use **Data Collection Health > Catalyst Center > Scheduled Reports - Configuration vs Observed Data** to confirm the configured mode, observed `report_name`, assigned sourcetype, event count, and last event. * Existing Custom API inputs that use an Advanced endpoint continue to work and remain visible when edited. * Forward `_internal` logs from heavy forwarders to the search tier to populate collector ownership and locally installed TA version/build fields in Data Collection Health. * Recommended for Splunk Enterprise 10.6 deployments or any environment planning a Python 3.13 runtime upgrade. On Splunk 10.0/10.1, runtime selection continues to use `python.version = python3`; `python.required` takes effect only on Splunk 10.2+.


Short Description:
Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk collects and normalizes API telemetry from Cisco Catalyst Center, SD-WAN (vManage), ISE, and Cyber Vision through modular inputs. It includes CIM-aligned knowledge objects, backward-compatible DNAC/Catalyst sourcetype coverage, and built-in health monitoring for input status, errors, and API load.

Description:
The IPinfo Splunk app brings IPinfo's API and IP database (MMDB) products into Splunk. It adds the ipinfo command, which looks up IP information for any IP address in your data. The app enriches Splunk events with geolocation, ASN, privacy, company, abuse, domains, carrier, and residential proxy data. It supports REST API and local MMDB lookups, with automated and manual database updates. SUPPORTED VERSIONS Supports Splunk Enterprise 9.x and 10.x and Splunk Cloud, on Windows, Linux, and Mac. Standalone, distributed, and search head cluster deployments are all supported. DATA PRODUCTS The app supports all IPinfo data types: - IP to Location - IP to Location Extended - IP to Privacy Detection - IP to Privacy Detection Extended - ASN - IP to Company - IP to Carrier - Hosted Domains - Abuse Contact - IP to Country ASN (free) - IP to Residential Proxy (7-day and 30-day lookback) It also supports IPinfo data products that will include different data types together (more info on ipinfo.io/pricing): - IPinfo Lite: Free, unlimited country-level geolocation and ASN data. Full accuracy, commercial license included, production-ready. - IPinfo Core: Adds city and region geolocation, lat/lon, timezone, postal, and boolean flags for anonymous, mobile, satellite and hosting IPs. - IPinfo Plus: Adds Privacy Extended: VPN, proxy, Tor, relay, hosting and mobile carrier identification with service name when applicable, geolocation radius, and ASN/geo last-changed timestamps. - IPinfo Max: Adds residential proxy detection with provider name, last seen, and percentage of days seen. Also includes last-seen dates for other anonymizer services. API only. USAGE After setup, analysts can run single IP lookups from the IPinfo tab or use full SPL syntax to enrich IPs in logs and dashboards. With local MMDB files, lookups are fast and have no request limits. The ipinfo command supports parameters for privacy, ASN, company, abuse, domains, carrier, country ASN, residential proxy, and a combined alltypes flag. GETTING STARTED Sign up at ipinfo.io and retrieve your access token from the dashboard. Start for free with IPinfo Lite: unlimited country-level geolocation and ASN data, full accuracy, and a commercial license so you can run it in production. Upgrade to Core, Plus, or Max as your use case grows. USE CASES - Account takeover and fraud detection - SOC alert enrichment and triage - Threat investigation and incident response - Detection rule engineering - Geo-fencing and compliance RESOURCES - Documentation: https://ipinfo.io/developers/splunk - Sign up: https://ipinfo.io/signup - Pricing: https://ipinfo.io/pricing - Enterprise plans: https://ipinfo.io/enterprise KEYWORDS IP geolocation, IP enrichment, proxy detection, VPN detection, residential proxy, fraud detection, SIEM enrichment, ASN lookup, account takeover, anonymizer detection

item.title: Ensign Akamai Web Security Add-on - v2.0.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
## Version 2.0.0 A major release. The add-on has been rebuilt on the current Splunk UCC framework (6.5.3), with substantial reliability, logging and security work. Upgrading from 1.0.9 is might supported and preserves your existing accounts, proxies and inputs. Let me know if it is not supported or you might encounter a problem for migrate into this new Version. ### Upgrade notes * **Restart Splunk after installing.** The add-on registers REST handlers and a modular input. * **Hard-refresh your browser** (Ctrl+Shift+R) after the restart so the new Configuration UI loads. * **New "Sourcetype" input field**, defaulting to `ensign_akamaisiem`. Earlier releases wrote events under `akamaisiem`, which did not match the bundled `props.conf`. If you built searches, dashboards or CIM mappings against `akamaisiem`, either point them at `ensign_akamaisiem` or set the Sourcetype field back to `akamaisiem` per input. * **Default index is now `main`** for newly created inputs. Existing inputs keep their configured index. * **First run collects history.** The new *Initial Lookback (hours)* setting defaults to 1 hour, so a newly created input backfills the last hour instead of starting at "now". Set it to 0 to keep the previous behaviour. * **Checkpoints now live in the KV Store** instead of a file inside the add-on directory. Existing file-based cursors are not read; each input resumes from its Initial Lookback window on the first run after upgrade. ### New * **Monitoring Dashboard** — overview, data ingestion, errors, and resource consumption panels for the add-on. * **Configurable sourcetype** per input. * **Initial Lookback (hours)** — seeds the first collection from Akamai's time-based mode (0–12 hours; Akamai retains 12). * **Gap recovery on an expired cursor.** An expired offset (HTTP 416) now replays the lookback window using time-based mode and then resumes offset mode, instead of silently skipping the gap. * **Full configuration reference** — every configuration file ships a detailed `.spec` plus a worked `.conf.example`, and `README/LOG-REFERENCE.txt` documents the internal logging in full. ### Reliability * **Bounded retry with exponential backoff** for connection errors, timeouts and 5xx responses, honouring `Retry-After` on HTTP 429 rate limits. * **Explicit request timeouts** (10s connect, 120s read) so a stalled Akamai edge can no longer hang the modular input indefinitely. * **Multi-page drain** — a single run collects up to 20 pages. Reaching that cap is logged rather than passing silently. * **Akamai's trailing summary record** (`{"total": N, "offset": "..."}`) is now recognised and dropped at the source, taking its cursor, instead of being indexed as an event. * **Proxy enforcement is fail-closed.** If a proxy is selected but disabled or unreadable, the run aborts and says why, rather than quietly connecting direct. * **Remote DNS Resolution now works.** The setting previously had no effect; it now selects the remote-resolving SOCKS scheme (`socks5h` / `socks4a`). * **Checkpoints in the KV Store**, replicated across a Search Head Cluster (if you installed this add-ons on Search Head Cluster, might try this). Implementation on Search Head Cluster is doable for now, but it is recommended if you put this at Ingestion Tier or Forwarder Tier. ### Logging * Internal logging is now one **5W1H `AUDIT key=value` record per event**, in a consistent field order (what / who / when / where / why / how / summary), so a single search works across every input. * **Log level takes effect on the next interval** — no Splunk restart required. * **DEBUG adds `stage=` dumps** for troubleshooting: resolved configuration, the outgoing request, a truncated response body, a transformed sample record, and cursor activity. These never appear above DEBUG. * **Fields are extracted at index time**, so they are searchable from a Search Head that does not have this add-on installed — the usual forwarder/indexer layout. ### Security * EdgeGrid tokens, proxy passwords, `Authorization` headers, `EG1-HMAC-SHA256` signatures and Splunk session keys are **redacted from every log line**. Where an operator needs to identify which key is in use, only `first4...last4` is written. * Credentials are read through **solnlib's ConfManager** rather than an undocumented REST parameter, and a value that reads back masked is refused. * Log values are sanitised, so a crafted HTTP header cannot forge audit fields. * **No architecture-specific binaries** are shipped: the package contains no compiled extensions and runs identically on Linux and Windows. ### Fixed * Events were written under a sourcetype the bundled `props.conf` did not target, so JSON parsing, timestamp extraction, field aliases, the geo lookup and the summary-record filter all silently did nothing. * The account and proxy configuration files were missing from `default/`, so the REST handlers had nothing to read on a fresh install and the Configuration page failed to load. * The default index was `default`, which is not a valid index name. * `README` documented a configuration file that does not exist, while the two real ones had no specification at all. * The `VERSION` file contained the version twice. * Version metadata is now generated from a single source, so `app.conf`, `app.manifest`, `VERSION`, `globalConfig.json` and `openapi.json` cannot disagree. ### Dependencies Built on **UCC framework 6.5.3**. Updated: `edgegrid-python` 2.0.7, `splunk-sdk` 3.0.0, `splunktaucclib` 8.2.0, `solnlib` 8.1.0, `charset-normalizer` 3.4.9 (pure-Python), `requests` 2.32.4, `idna` 3.16, `certifi` 2026.5.20. `urllib3` is pinned to 1.26.20 for Splunk 9.x compatibility. ### Compatibility Splunk Enterprise 9.x and 10.x, Splunk Cloud. Python 3.9 and 3.13 (`python.required = 3.9, 3.13`).


Short Description:
Captures Akamai security events via SIEM Integration API v1. Built on Splunk UCC with multi-account, multi-proxy, and encrypted credential support.


Description:
Ensign Akamai Web Security Add-on for Splunk An enterprise-grade alternative to the official Akamai SIEM app, rebuilt by adopt Splunk UCC Framework. WHY THIS ADD-ON? The official Akamai app (refer to : https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4310) uses legacy way for enabled the input (via Settings => Data Input) and several parsing is not key-value-pair based after coming ingested in Splunk, rather than using spath and makes easier for analyst to choose the fields, this add-ons are one to solve that. This add-on provides: - Full UI-driven configuration based on your usual for inputs based on Add-ons (just directly configured under the add-ons like the other Splunk Supported Add-ons). - Multi-account management with encrypted credential storage via Splunk's native password vault - Multi-proxy support (HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS4, SOCKS5) with per-input proxy assignment - Offset-based checkpointing for reliable data continuity across restarts. - Custom sourcetype override per input for seamless migration. - Deployment Server compatible. DATA SOURCE: Captures security events from Akamai SIEM Integration API v1, supporting: - App & API Protector - Kona Site Defender - Web Application Protector - Client Reputation - Bot Manager - Account Protector EVENT PROCESSING: - URL-decodes all fields recursively - Parses HTTP headers into structured key-value pairs - Decodes base64-encoded attackData rule fields into structured objects - Drops summary/offset metadata events (nullQueue) Ref: https://techdocs.akamai.com/siem-integration/docs Built by Ensign Infosecurity Indonesia.

Release Notes:
**Version 0.9.0 (July 22nd, 2026)** - **IMPORTANT / BREAKING CHANGE:** The Oracle SBC media-flow fields have been renamed to align with Oracle's own terminology. The old "west", "east", "extra_west" and "extra_east" field-name prefixes were a nonstandard naming scheme that did not appear anywhere in Oracle's documentation. The new names map to Oracle's flow-set and flow-direction concepts — Flow-Set 1 or 2 (fs1 / fs2), and Forward or Reverse (fwd / rev). For the media flow and quality-of-service fields the mapping is: - `west_*` → `fs1_fwd_*` (Flow-Set 1, Forward direction) - `east_*` → `fs1_rev_*` (Flow-Set 1, Reverse direction) - `extra_*` → `fs2_fwd_*` / `fs2_rev_*` (Flow-Set 2, Forward / Reverse) A few groups of fields do not follow that prefix pattern exactly: the media-stop-time and RTP transmitted-byte/packet counters are indexed by flow-set and calling/called party, and the session R-Factor and MOS values are now simply `calling_r_factor`, `calling_mos`, `called_r_factor` and `called_mos` (they are session-level, not per-flow). If you have built any of your own saved searches, dashboards, or reports that reference the old field names, you will need to update them when you upgrade. - Added a new search command, `| checksbcflowfieldnames`, to make that migration easy and exact. Run it (as an admin, or as a user with the `admin_all_objects` capability, for a complete picture) and it will itemize every place in your Splunk knowledge objects, ie saved searches, dashboards, macros, event types, data models, etc, that still reference any old field name, giving you the precise new name to use for each one. - Call detail view for Oracle SBC calls now includes a single-row summary table at the top echoing top level details like ingress/egress realm, time, disposition and duration etc. - Call detail view for Oracle SBC calls now includes a CallFlowGraph module that presents a DAG visualization of the various ip addresses and ingress/egress realms involved in the B2BUA signaling and media flow.

item.title: Analyst1 - v1.6.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
## New Features * **Hit Stats "Outputs" management UI:** a dedicated dashboard to create, edit, preview, run, and copy Hit Stats outputs without hand-editing saved searches. Includes inline Validate/Preview, an Actions menu, support for data-model / `tstats` (leading-pipe) base searches, a configurable Dimension 1 *Source Field*, and an optional Dimension 3 context field. * **Hit Stats historical backfill:** a new `analyst1hitstatsbackfill` command backfills past Hit Stats using memory-safe streaming reads and per-day uploads, so a newly configured output can populate history rather than only going forward. * **Analyst1 Monitoring dashboard:** a unified view of all three sync pipelines (API to KV, API to Index, Index to KV) with recent-run health, lineage, reconciliation counts, per-run error drill-down, and four built-in alerts. * **New operator commands:** * `analyst1forcesync`: trigger an on-demand full indicator sync. * `analyst1indexcutover`: migrate an index-mode deployment to KV mode and retire the legacy lookup-update searches. * `analyst1clearindicators`: clear synced indicators from KV/ES (replaces the prior `analyst1clearesthreatintel`). * **Remote Splunk KV support:** indicator sync can write to a remote Splunk KV store (with TLS verification and proxy support), enabling deployments where the collecting node and the KV store are separate. *** ## Bug Fixes * **Configured ES push could silently no-op.** When an ES lookup was configured but the target ES collection was missing, the sync reported success even though nothing was written to ES. That condition now fails loudly so it is visible instead of silently skipped. * **Validating or saving an account could interrupt a running sync.** Saving or validating an Analyst1 account revoked the account's active token; if a sync was in flight it would be 401'd mid-fetch. Validation now uses a separate concurrent token and no longer revokes the live one. * **Hit Stats "Summary" mode mis-counted.** Summary mode de-duplicated to one arbitrary row per indicator instead of summing by day, so multi-row or multi-day searches under-reported or mis-reported counts. Summary mode now sums counts per day (matching Basic mode). *** ## Improvements & Updates * **Indicator sync engine hardening:** a re-architected stage, route, prove, apply pipeline with per-type isolation and full-read completeness gating. Deletes are skipped when a read is incomplete, preventing accidental removal of indicators after a partial fetch. * **Observability overhaul:** unified sync lifecycle telemetry across all three pipelines, correlation IDs, and accurate write counters (index-mode writes are no longer reported as KV writes). This data feeds the new Monitoring dashboard. * **OAuth streamlining:** proactive token refresh with bounded retry, a guaranteed fresh token before large (>100 MB) streaming Hit Stats uploads, and removal of obsolete single-token machinery. * **Hit Stats upload reliability:** scheduled outputs are spread out (schedule skew) to avoid burst-induced 503s when many fire at once, with retry and backoff hardening and idempotent per-day replace semantics. * **Fail-loud on storage errors:** KV batch write and delete failures now fail the run visibly instead of being silently swallowed. * **Search Head Cluster hardening:** more reliable captain detection and mutual-exclusion locking for the upgrade migration. * Configuration and documentation cleanups and consistent dashboard theming. *** ## Test Coverage 1.6.0 was validated with an automated unit suite plus an Ansible-driven integration harness exercised on disposable Splunk labs. **Unit tests:** 1,000+ automated unit tests (58 modules) covering sync strategies, KV and index targets, IOC transformation, OAuth token lifecycle, locking, and migrations. **Platform matrix:** Splunk **9.4.12** and **10.2**, on both **single-instance** and **Search Head Cluster** topologies (plus Heavy-Forwarder collection). **Scenarios exercised:** * **Fresh install** and **in-place 1.5.9 to 1.6.0 upgrade**, on a standalone instance and on a dedicated ephemeral Search Head Cluster (with aged pre-upgrade state and the account migration). * **Sync modes:** KV mode and index mode; the API to KV, API to Index, and Index to KV (relay) pipelines; incremental (DIFF) and full (FULL) syncs; a standalone 2x2 sync matrix. * **Data-integrity and parity gates:** exact match of ES `*_intel` value-sets against KV after sync; index-to-KV relay verified against the API-sync "gold standard"; ingestion route-map consistency; a regression guard that a failed sync must not advance its cursor. * **Remote Splunk:** a REST-only remote-Splunk suite (install, configure, verify, diff) and remote-KV write mode (TLS verify, proxy, plus negative and scoped-role permission cases). * **Search Head Cluster specifics:** config replication, captain-gated migration, rolling-restart drain, and single-execution behavior. * **Hit Stats:** upload path via proxy, resilience (skew and retry), and preview and validation. * **On-demand Analyst1 sensor config change** (diff-trigger) end-to-end.

Under SCP2 (`chunked = true`), Splunk decides distribution from the SDK's getinfo response, not `commands.conf`, so the `local = true` setting added in 1.1.0 was ignored. The command now reports itself search-head-only by default, so prepending `| localop` is no longer needed. * Store MaxMind databases in the app's `databases/` directory instead of `local/data/`. A directory of the app's own is outside search head cluster replication summaries and outside Splunk's default knowledge bundle allowlist, so replication of the databases is controlled entirely by the app, and the new path is resolved relative to the app root so it also works when the command runs from a knowledge bundle on an indexer. Databases found in the old location are moved to the new one automatically - by the updater's next run or by the first `geoip` search that would otherwise miss them - so upgrades keep working without waiting for a re-download. * Add opt-in support for running the `geoip` command on indexers. A new "Distributed Search" configuration tab provides a "Run on indexers" checkbox, off by default because large databases increase the knowledge bundle size and replication can exceed bundle size limits. Enabling it requires restarting the search head (every member, in a search head cluster), because Splunk only reads the replication rules that put the databases into the knowledge bundle at startup.

SA-Eventgen reads \`eventgen.conf\` only when it launches, so the app restarts the modular input after a change rather than leaving the new setting to be picked up whenever someone next restarts it by hand. No Splunk restart is involved. Because SA-Eventgen runs every sample in a single process, that restart briefly interrupts other running samples and resets \`integerid\` counters. \- Configuration is written through Splunk's own \`configs/conf-eventgen\` endpoint. Search head cluster replication for \`eventgen.conf\` is enabled by this app. \*\*Compatibility\*\* \- Requires SA-Eventgen on the same instance \- Requires the admin or sc\_admin role \- Event generation requires Linux or macOS on x86\_64. SA-Eventgen 8.2.1 ships compiled binaries for \`linux\_x86\_64\` and \`darwin\_x86\_64\` only — there is no Windows build and none for arm64. Release Notes:

  • Advance notice - all CUBE configuration will be removed from this app in the next release. If you index CUBE data, deploy the TA\_cube add-on to your forwarders and the SA\_cube app to your search heads, forwarders first, since index-time extractions cannot be applied retroactively. Today this app's copy shadows the one in SA\_cube, so fixes shipped there never reach you.
  • Added a health check, "Check whether you have CUBE data but are missing the SA\_cube app", so you are warned before that removal lands.
  • The "cube\_cdr\_compact" sourcetype no longer accepts new data. Its FIELD\_NAMES was wrong - Cisco's compact format is attributes 0-22 plus the 12-field feature block, not attributes 0-32 - so every column from 23 on was mislabeled. Send compact CDRs to the "cube\_cdr" sourcetype instead; attributes 0-22 are identical. The search-time keys are retained so data already indexed under the old sourcetype keeps rendering.
  • Fixed three bugs in how "duration" is calculated for CUBE data, along with cube\_duration, duration\_total, duration\_in\_minutes and dateTimeDisconnect. Durations will change for existing customers, because they were previously wrong. The digits were taken from tx\_duration with substr(x,0,len(x)-3), which drops the last digit rather than the "ms" suffix; we checked only that tx\_duration was non-empty, not that it looked like a duration, so on some routers it read an unrelated column; and the timestamp fallback required a leading "\*" that not all gateways emit. All three are fixed at index time and search time.
  • Added a health check, "Check that the CUBE CDR columns line up with the field names we give them". A CUBE CDR file has no header row, so names map to columns by position, and a router using "cdr-format compact" or a custom acct-template produces wrong values with no error. The check samples recent data and tests three columns with recognisable shapes.
  • Removed the "AutoHeader-ios-gateway-detailed" transform and the REPORT-AutoHeader keys that referenced it. It re-parsed the raw CSV line at search time to supply fields for CUBE data indexed before 7.7.1 (November 2024), which is redundant now that FIELD\_NAMES is in effect, and it was a second copy of the field list that had drifted out of step. If you still hold CUBE data indexed before November 2024, that data will lose its fields - contact us before upgrading.
  • FIELD\_NAMES for CUBE now covers all 133 Cisco attributes. Attributes 130-132 - mos\_qe, packet\_loss\_rate and out\_of\_order\_rate - are new; attributes 124-129 were wrongly named feature\_param11 through feature\_param16 and now carry their real names, ip\_phone\_info, ip\_pbx\_mode, in\_lpcor\_group, out\_lpcor\_group, fac\_digit and fac\_status.
  • Fixed the "activity" field for CUBE data, which keyed on a field name that only existed by way of the AutoHeader transform above.
  • Fixed gapfill\_with\_prediction, gapfill\_with\_redundancy and gapfill\_with\_silence, which through a copy-paste error were all calculated from gapfill\_with\_interpolation.
  • Removed the dead "AutoHeader-ios-gateway-compact" transform, which was defined but never referenced by anything.
  • Fixed three lookups that could never match CUBE data. "h323\_disconnect\_description" keyed on the decimal cause code where the router writes hex left-aligned in four characters; "info\_type\_description" keyed on the numeric information transfer capability where the router writes the word; and the codec lookup had no entry for opus, ilbc, isac, g722-64, gsmamrnb, t38 or the pre-ietf G.729 variants. The first of these is a column on the CUBE call detail page that was always blank. These are kept in step with SA\_cube, which owns them.
  • receive\_delay, round\_trip\_delay, hiwater\_playout\_delay and lowater\_playout\_delay in CUBE data are now numbers rather than strings such as "45 ms", so they can be averaged and charted. Values are milliseconds.
  • Removed bin/timeshifter\_and\_anonymizer.py from the package. It is one of our internal tools for building demo data and was never intended to ship; it has no effect on the app and nothing references it.


Description:
This commercial app is available as a 60 day trial and is compatible with both Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud. The app gives your team greatly increased visibility, monitoring, and reporting functionality around Cisco Unified Communications (aka CUCM / CallManager), whether you're a small organization with a hundred phones or one of the largest companies in the world. Whether troubleshooting individual calls or building high level reporting, it helps you visualize and understand in all areas: agents, users, and huntgroups; concurrency and utilization; call flow; call quality; call volume; devices; failed calls; locations and sites; and audits and compliance. Your team can trust it as their day-to-day tool for navigating call data from your Cisco CallManager deployment, and it can also become their main tool for building custom reports, alerts and dashboards around that data. This is true whether it’s a standard report you’d expect or a custom report that nothing else has been able to provide. Note that this isn't a package of content, but more a tank that allows you to drive around in your data. You won’t find a leftnav full of canned CDR reports to click on (that "don't quite fit"). Instead, you get an open flexible framework to investigate anything, drill down into anything, report on anything, over anything, by anything (occasionally with hands-on help from Sideview Support =). item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
* The "cube_cdr_compact" sourcetype has been removed. Its FIELD_NAMES was wrong - Cisco's compact format is attributes 0-22 plus the 12-field feature block, not attributes 0-32 - so every column from 23 on was mislabeled. Send compact CDRs to the "cube_cdr" sourcetype instead; attributes 0-22 are identical. We only support "cdr-format detailed" with no acct-template. * Fixed three bugs in the index-time "duration" field for CUBE data. Durations will change for existing customers, because they were previously wrong. The digits were taken from tx_duration with substr(x,0,len(x)-3), which drops the last digit rather than the "ms" suffix, making durations roughly ten times too short; we checked only that tx_duration was non-empty, not that it looked like a duration, so on some routers it read an unrelated column; and the timestamp fallback required a leading "*" that not all gateways emit. * FIELD_NAMES now covers all 133 Cisco file-accounting attributes, up from 130. Attributes 130-132 are new fields - mos_qe, packet_loss_rate and out_of_order_rate - which current IOS-XE releases emit and which we were discarding. * Attributes 124-129 were wrongly named feature_param11 through feature_param16. They are not part of the feature block at all, and now carry their real names: ip_phone_info, ip_pbx_mode, in_lpcor_group, out_lpcor_group, fac_digit and fac_status. If you built anything on the old names you will need to update it. * Added a field reference above the [cube_cdr] stanza in props.conf: all 133 Cisco file-accounting attributes in order, our names for them, and the router commands to verify your own boxes send this column set. A CUBE CDR file has no header row, so the mapping is positional and cannot be checked from the data alone.

Release Notes:
1.0.0 — First general-availability release Deploy an AWS Lambda into your own AWS account, entirely from the Splunk UI, that streams S3 objects into Splunk over HEC: S3 ObjectCreated -> Lambda -> HEC -> index. Deployment runs in-process against the AWS API (boto3) - no AWS console, no AWS CLI. AWS credentials are stored encrypted in Splunk and can be wiped automatically once the Lambda is created. Nothing in the add-on or the deployed Lambda ever calls the vendor: license verification is fully offline. WHAT'S INCLUDED \- One-click deploy of the ingest Lambda (IAM role, function, reserved concurrency, S3 ObjectCreated notification). Preview shows the exact AWS calls before anything is created. \- Compression auto-detected from content, not from the file name: gzip, zstd, bzip2 or uncompressed. Everything is streamed, so memory does not grow with object size. \- Object layout auto-detected: \* line-oriented - NDJSON, syslog, CSV, ALB / CloudFront / VPC Flow Logs, S3 access logs. One line per event; no line is dropped. \* JSON envelope {"Records":\[...]} - CloudTrail, AWS Config, GuardDuty - and bare JSON arrays. One event per element, streamed element by element. \- Routing table: map key prefixes to their own index and sourcetype (longest prefix wins), so one deployment feeds many log types. A route can post to HEC /raw so the sourcetypes the Splunk Add-on for AWS already ships do the line breaking and field extraction, and can skip a header line (VPC Flow Logs). \- Recovery from a lapsed subscription: objects refused while the license is expired are recorded, and "Recover missed objects" replays exactly those objects after renewal - no duplicates. \- Air-gapped support: corporate proxy for AWS API egress, and an exportable self-contained deploy script (Lambda binary embedded) for Splunk hosts with no AWS connectivity. \- Hourly license\_status events (sourcetype s3\_lambda\_deployer:license) so you can alert on expiry with your own saved searches. REQUIREMENTS \- A valid license key (this is a paid add-on). Enter it on the Licensing tab. Keys are node-locked to your AWS account id. \- Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud with an enabled HEC endpoint reachable from AWS Lambda, and a token whose allowed indexes cover your target index. \- AWS credentials with permission to create the IAM role, Lambda function and bucket notification. They are needed only at deploy time - the deployed Lambda runs on its own IAM role. KNOWN LIMITATION \- If the license stays expired longer than your S3 bucket's retention / lifecycle period, AWS deletes those objects and that data cannot be recovered into Splunk. Align your renewal with the bucket lifecycle. Support: [support@innosw.net](mailto:support@innosw.net)


Short Description:
Deploy a serverless S3-to-Splunk pipeline into your own AWS account, right from the Splunk UI. An event-driven Go Lambda streams and gunzips new S3 objects to your HEC endpoint in real time — no Heavy Forwarder, no polling, no idle infrastructure. Works on Splunk Cloud and Enterprise.


Description:
Inno Streaming Add-on for AWS S3 lets a Splunk administrator deploy a serverless ingestion pipeline into their own AWS account directly from the Splunk UI — no AWS console, no aws CLI, and no forwarder in the data path. The problem: getting S3 data into Splunk usually means standing up and maintaining polling-based inputs or Heavy Forwarders, granting broad AWS access, and paying for idle infrastructure. This add-on replaces that with an event-driven, in-account design. How it works: you enter your AWS credentials (stored encrypted in Splunk), your HEC endpoint, target index, and S3 bucket, then click Deploy. Using the AWS API (boto3), the add-on provisions a least-privilege IAM role, a compiled Go Lambda, and an S3 ObjectCreated notification. From then on, every object that lands in the bucket triggers the Lambda, which streams and decompresses the object and forwards the records to your Splunk HEC endpoint in real time. Data flows S3 → Lambda → HEC entirely inside your AWS account; it never passes through the vendor. Highlights: - Deploy from the Splunk UI in minutes; idempotent re-deploys. - Event-driven and serverless — the Lambda scales with your data and back to zero when idle. - Installs on Splunk Cloud search heads and on Splunk Enterprise / Heavy Forwarders. - AWS keys are only needed at deploy time and are auto-wiped after a successful deploy; the Lambda runs on its own IAM role. - Compression auto-detected from the content, not the file name: gzip, zstd, bzip2 or uncompressed — all streamed, so memory does not grow with object size. - Two object layouts, auto-detected: * line-oriented — NDJSON / JSON Lines and plain-text logs (syslog, CSV, key=value, ALB / CloudFront access logs, VPC Flow Logs, S3 access logs). One line, one event. * JSON envelope {"Records":[...]} and bare JSON arrays — CloudTrail, AWS Config, GuardDuty. One event per element, streamed element by element, so a CloudTrail file with 100k records never lands in memory at once. - Routing table: map key prefixes to their own index and sourcetype, so one deployment feeds many log types. A route can post to HEC /raw and reuse the sourcetypes the Splunk Add-on for AWS already ships for line breaking and field extraction. - Compiled Go Lambda binary, corporate-proxy support, and an air-gapped export option for Splunk hosts with no AWS connectivity. Requires an HEC endpoint reachable from AWS Lambda and a token whose allowed indexes cover your target index. The add-on is free to install. A license key is required to preview, export or deploy; keys are node-locked to your AWS account id and verified entirely offline. See detailed performance-benchmark results (measured S3-to-HEC throughput and tuning), step-by-step usage guides, full documentation, and licensing at https://innosw.net - 11 USD / month - 110 USD / year

Release Notes:
Version 1.0.1 - reliability and compatibility fixes. Forward compatibility: restmap.conf now declares python.required (3.9, 3.13) alongside python.version, clearing the Splunk 10.2+ deprecation of python.version. No change to supported versions - the app still targets Splunk Enterprise 9.1 through 10.x, search heads only, and python.required is ignored below 10.2. Write path fixes: * Settings and record writes now use the correct splunkd request transport and KV Store upsert semantics, so first-time writes (including the initial settings save on a fresh install) succeed. * \- The app REST endpoint is now exposed at all nested route depths, so the full change workflow (validate, approve, publish, roll back) resolves through Splunk Web. * \- Request bodies are delivered reliably through Splunk Web's proxy. * \- The audit hash-chain tip is resolved deterministically, independent of KV Store sort ordering. Install and first-use fixes: * Removed a setup gate that could leave a fresh install unable to reach the app views. The Setup page remains available from the navigation bar. * \- A brand-new lookup with no existing baseline now diffs cleanly instead of surfacing a raw splunkd error. Validated on Splunk Enterprise 9.4 with KV Store; AppInspect clean. Requires a Splunk restart after install to register the REST handler and KV Store collections.


Short Description:
Air-gap-first governance for Splunk lookup changes: inventory, deterministic validation, semantic diff, approvals with separation of duties, verified publication and rollback, audit evidence export, offline transfer bundles, and optional behind-the-firewall AI review with zero authority. No cloud dependencies. No telemetry.


Description:
Federal AI LookupOps turns Splunk lookup edits into governed changes. It is built air-gap-first: no cloud dependencies, no external services, and no telemetry. Analysts propose candidate changes by uploading a CSV, pasting records, or cloning the current lookup. A deterministic policy engine validates schemas, unique and composite keys, field types (IPv4, IPv6, CIDR, hostname, URL, email, date, boolean, number), enumerations, patterns, blank values, duplicates, and expirations. A key-aware semantic diff shows exactly what will change - additions, removals, field-level modifications, normalization-only changes, and schema changes - each with a stable evidence ID. Approvers act under enforced separation of duties; self-approval is blocked server-side. Publication captures the production content hash at submission, re-verifies it immediately before the write, publishes only through documented Splunk interfaces, verifies the resulting hash after the write, and preserves the previous version for one-action verified rollback. Every step lands in a hash-chained audit trail with an exportable JSON evidence report. Deterministic offline bundles with SHA-256 manifests move changes safely between enclaves. Optionally, connect a customer-approved, behind-the-firewall LLM (OpenAI-compatible, Ollama, or custom JSON). AI review runs server-side only with TLS verification always enforced, and provides risk assessment, justification-vs-diff contradiction detection, reviewer questions, policy proposals, normalization patches, dependency impact, and release narratives. Every material AI finding must cite deterministic evidence IDs, and the model has zero authority - it can never approve, publish, or roll back. Works with your existing SAML login through Splunk's own authentication. Includes role-based capabilities (view, submit, approve, publish, rollback, AI use, AI admin), KV Store-backed state that replicates across search-head clusters, and full documentation.
